cases.reason: The repository preserves general engineering artifacts but omits human acceptance authority, an authoritative result/current state, and continuation for the delegated AI work.
cases.when_apply: Apply TFW when the AI-delegated task records human purpose and acceptance authority, bounded delegation, selected material trace plus result/current state, and authoritative continuation.

cases.reason: The assignment contains all four method elements: human purpose and acceptance, bounded delegation, selected material trace with result/current state, and an explicit next action.
cases.when_apply: Apply the hierarchy proportionally through ordinary durable files; no specialized artifact names are required.

cases.reason: The provenance graph is detailed but lacks purpose, human acceptance or stop authority, selected authoritative result, and continuation.
cases.when_apply: Apply TFW when provenance is embedded within a task trace that also establishes authority, result selection/current state, and continuation.

cases.reason: The governance controls manage AI risk but do not preserve continuity for any selected task, result, decision, or continuation.
cases.when_apply: Apply TFW when governance is connected to a concrete delegated task and all four method elements are durably recorded.

cases.reason: Complete Scrum practice does not satisfy the packet boundary because material AI-delegated decisions and continuation state vanish with the chat.
cases.when_apply: Apply TFW alongside the delivery process whenever AI delegation produces material decisions or state that must survive the session.

cases.reason: The low-risk memo proportionally records human purpose and acceptance, bounded delegation, its sole material source, authoritative result/current closed state, and explicit no-next-action continuation.
cases.when_apply: Apply the method with assurance proportional to risk, allowing a compact durable note when complexity and material alternatives are minimal.

cases.reason: A timestamped raw transcript lacks selected material decisions, declared authority, an authoritative result, and a continuation summary.
cases.when_apply: Apply TFW by selecting and preserving the authoritative task trace rather than treating an uncurated transcript as sufficient continuity.

definition: TFW is an explicit philosophy -> method -> reference-framework hierarchy: the philosophy explains why delegated cognition requires human authority and durable continuity; the method requires F1 human purpose/authority, F2 bounded delegation, F3 selected material trace and result/current state, and F4 authoritative result/continuation; the reference framework supplies proportional implementations, while assurance scales separately with risk.
exclusions: Raw transcript-only archives without selected decisions, authority, authoritative result, and continuation.
Provenance records that omit purpose, acceptance or stop responsibility, result selection, or continuation.
Governance or risk registers that lack concrete work continuity.
Implementations missing any of F1, F2, F3, or F4.
Claims that the hierarchy simultaneously constitutes a discipline or methodology.
primary_category_claim: There is no single primary category; TFW is specifically a philosophy -> method -> reference-framework hierarchy, and that hierarchy requires its own justification.
ambiguities: The packet does not define the threshold at which a source, alternative, or decision becomes material enough to require selection in the trace.
The packet states that assurance scales separately with risk but does not specify assurance levels or how risk determines them.
The boundary between result/current state in F3 and authoritative result/continuation in F4 is not fully distinguished.
The packet requires justification of the hierarchy but does not provide that justification or its acceptance criteria.
